questions.question: The driver's own row (route = openrouter, role = orchestrate, rung 1): Pro at effort high or Pro at effort medium?
questions.recommendation: Pro high, measured against Pro medium over the first five driver sessions by evidence report ladder
questions.default: Pro medium as rung 1 (the seat's saved default today), Pro high as rung 2, claude/orchestrate (fable high) as rung 3 — what SD1 writes; an answer of high swaps rungs 1 and 2 in one row edit

questions.question: Anthropic models on OpenRouter as ladder rungs: add rows or keep the hold?
questions.recommendation: Keep the hold; the claude rungs stay printed launch lines for the operator's Claude Code session and the report's escalate column shows whether they are ever reached
questions.default: Hold — no openrouter row names an Anthropic model

questions.question: The technical class: derived from touches, or a third field in the typed heading?
questions.recommendation: Derived from touches through docs/ledger/task-classes.toml (nothing new to type; the heading regex, the orchestrator guard's HEADING_ERE and the harness skill untouched)

headings: ### SD1 (code, M) — the ladder in the routing table: rung and fallback rows, class in the key, factory_route and route.py in lockstep, the first rungs marked unmeasured
### SD2 (code, S) — the technical class: task-classes.toml, one primary class per task from touches, the class in the brief and the json
### SD3 (code, M) — the driver climbs: the rung from the key, --prior carries the failed attempt, class and rung in the result, a claude rung prints its launch line
### SD4 (code, S) — the drive job: seat-submit drive resolves the orchestrate row, refuses the shared home, --wait polls a spooled job; seat-run runs drive as web
### SD5 (code, M) — the spool: seat-spool.path starts one seat@ per validated job, the drive job on the unit, the unit PATH for the driving verbs, asserted in seat-eval and seat-vm
### SD6 (code, M) — one rule file: docs/ledger/guard-rules.toml holds the protected paths, the verb families and the history rules; the orchestrator guard reads it
### SD7 (code, M) — hook-guard reads the shared rule file: the token-scan arm, parity with the orchestrator guard over the sweep fixture
### SD8 (code, S) — the record answers the operator: rung, class, prior and escalate in the tasks row, evidence report ladder refused under five
### SD9 (docs, S) — the driving skill: brief, dispatch, gate, integrate as calls to the driver scripts; what the driver decides alone
### SD10 (docs, S) — the seat-driver runbook: seed the drive home, submit, open, the four verbs, the spool, rollback
